claims: C1 the assistant must strive to follow all applicable instructions when producing a response
C2 applicable instructions include all system, developer and user instructions
C3 an instruction is excluded from the must-follow set if it conflicts with a higher-authority instruction
C4 an instruction is excluded from the must-follow set if it conflicts with a later instruction at the same authority

concepts.name: applicable_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that applies to the current request, determined by filtering candidate instructions

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

concepts.name: system_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from the system level of the authority hierarchy
concepts.inference: the clause names system, developer and user instructions as categories; each category must be represented as a predicate about instructions

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from the developer level of the authority hierarchy
concepts.inference: the clause names system, developer and user instructions as categories; each category must be represented as a predicate about instructions

concepts.name: user_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from the user level of the authority hierarchy
concepts.inference: the clause names system, developer and user instructions as categories; each category must be represented as a predicate about instructions

concepts.name: instruction_authority
concepts.gloss: instruction I is at authority level L of the hierarchy
concepts.inference: comparing authority between instructions requires each instruction to have an authority level

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: instruction I conflicts with instruction J, meaning they cannot both be followed consistently
concepts.inference: the clause's exception is defined by conflict between instructions; which pairs conflict is a fact about the case

concepts.name: instruction_order
concepts.gloss: instruction I appears later in the conversation than instruction J
concepts.inference: the clause's exception for a later instruction at the same authority requires an ordering among instructions

concepts.name: excluded_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an applicable instruction that is excluded from the must-follow set because it conflicts with a higher-authority instruction or a later instruction at the same authority
concepts.inference: the clause defines an exception to the obligation; the exception is captured by this derived predicate

ontology.gloss: I is an applicable instruction because it is a system, developer, or user instruction
I is an applicable instruction because it is a system, developer, or user instruction
I is an applicable instruction because it is a system, developer, or user instruction
I is excluded because it conflicts with a higher-authority instruction
ontology.body: applicable_instruction(I), conflicts_with(I, J), instruction_authority(I, L1), instruction_authority(J, L2), authority_levels_hierarchy(L2, L1)

ontology.gloss: I is excluded because it conflicts with a later instruction at the same authority
ontology.body: applicable_instruction(I), conflicts_with(I, J), instruction_authority(I, L), instruction_authority(J, L), instruction_order(J, I)

asserts.read_back: following instruction % is obligatory when it is applicable and not excluded by a higher-authority or later same-authority conflict

closure.reason: the clause imposes a positive obligation to follow applicable instructions; silence about an instruction does not permit ignoring it, so the default for this act class is closed unless an exception applies
